text:
A lightweight 2.5D character player for the web, with lip sync and webcam face tracking. A few lines of code put a character in a page, a stream overlay or an app. 
 Comes with 23 featured characters in different styles, ready to use.
 

 English · 中文 · 日本語 · Tiếng Việt 

 

- WebGL2, no dependencies, about 30 KB gzipped for the core
- Lip sync (microphone, audio, video) and webcam face tracking (MediaPipe), both in the browser, imported only when you need them
- Plays LivLiv, VRM and PNGTuber characters through the same API
- Full-body characters stand on the ground: they sway, crouch and dip with their feet in place, in the shot you pick
- 23 featured characters in characters/ , ready to use

 Try it

- Online : the examples run on livliv-dev.github.io/player.
- Here : npm install && npm run build , serve this folder with any static server and open /example/demo.html 
 (expressions, actions, microphone, camera; ?model=../characters/ / picks another character).
 /example/png.html and /example/vrm.html show a PNGTuber and a VRM.
- On livliv.ai : each character's page there plays it with the same renderer. Start at
 livliv.ai/discover.

 Project LivLiv

We want the art of creating characters to belong to everyone.

We're open-sourcing our AI tools for character creation, the player and its playback protocol,
and a stage where your characters can meet an audience.

Come say hello on Discord and follow us on X (Twitter).

 Use it in your page

 

 

Lip sync and face tracking:

 

A VRM or a PNGTuber, on the same API:

 

The whole API is in API.md: options, params, expressions and actions, feel settings, drivers, recorded poses and attachment
points, VRM and PNGTuber characters, the limits on untrusted files, the model package and the format version. The LivLiv package format ( .livliv ,
 model.json v4) is in FORMAT.md, with a JSON Schema in schema/ ; packages exported before v4
are described in FORMAT-v3.md and still play.

 New in 0.6: long hair swings below the shoulders as the head and body move (a model's tuning.hair sway sets how
far; 0 turns it off), and long hair lying on the body goes with the body, not the head ( tuning.hair rest ). Blinks no
longer show a see-through iris halfway. A character's feel settings ( tuning : how far it turns, how freely its hair
swings, how often it blinks …) can be read with player.tuning and changed while it plays with player.setTuning() ,
for an editor's sliders, and load(source, { continueMotion: true }) keeps a character moving when an edit loads it
again. VRM files exported from Blender play. Code that runs its own frame loop can take the renderer itself from an
advanced entry, @livliv-dev/player/runtime . Pages written for 0.5 need no change. See Feel
settings in API.md.

 The npm package is the player alone. The featured characters are in this repository's characters/ : copy
 the ones you use next to your page, with their licence.

 Featured characters

 characters/ holds 23 characters, ready to load() . Most were made by LivLiv: use them free with credit
("Characters: LivLiv (livliv.ai)"), commercially too if you are an individual. Don't sell them or merchandise made from
them, and don't train AI models on them. They are not covered by the Apache License; the terms are in
characters/LICENSE.md. Kujira, Kujira Q and Pen come from other people's work, with their own
terms in characters/CREDITS.md.

 New in 0.5.0: full-body characters. Drawn head to feet, they stand on the ground: they sway, crouch and dip while
their feet stay put. Four featured characters are full-body: Tsubaki, Neve, Juno and Viola (f05–f08). Pick the shot
with player.view.fit : 'frame' (default), 'knee' or 'whole' ; see
Full-body characters in API.md.

Each character has a cover.webp , its first frame: player.load(source, { poster }) shows it until the character is
ready, and example/loading.js shows it before any script has run.

Each character is also one file to download, .livliv , at .livliv 
(the names below link to them). They are served with CORS, so a page on another site can load() one straight from
there, and index.json lists them all.

 Characters of your own

You can bring in a PNGTuber's pictures, or a VRM (drawn with three.js); or make a character of your own from one
picture on livliv.ai.

- A PNGTuber : two pictures (mouth closed, mouth open), and two more with the eyes closed if you have them.
- A VRM : from VRoid Studio or any tool that exports VRM 0.x or 1.0.
- A LivLiv model : make one from a picture on livliv.ai, then download its model package from
 the character's page ( Model package ): a .livliv file. Pass it to load() as it is (a URL, or the File 
 someone picked), or unzipped as a folder. Full-body characters play too (from 0.5); livliv.ai does not offer their
 packages yet.

 About the player and the characters

LivLiv Player and the .livliv format are LivLiv's own work. They use no Live2D software or Cubism SDK and do not
read .moc3 or .cmo3 files. "Live2D" is a trademark of Live2D Inc.; LivLiv is not affiliated with it.

Making a character on livliv.ai uses AI. The player itself only plays: it calls no AI service and reads only the files
you point it at. Face tracking runs Google's MediaPipe in the browser, and camera images stay on the device; API.md has
the networking details.

The featured characters in this repository were made on LivLiv too, also with AI; Kujira, Kujira Q and Pen adapt other
people's characters (credits). Refined Nana ( d03ft ) also has
swinging parts and head-turn keyforms added with LivLiv's own tools.

A package's meta.author and meta.license record who made it and on what term
